Surah al-Nazi'at (The Pullers Out) is Meccan.

[Narrated by Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Nazi'at was revealed in Makkah." See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/403.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿By those who pull out violently﴾ — meaning the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers from their bodies, just as a puller draws the bowstring to its full extent (ighraq) after he has drawn it, until when it is almost released he lets it return into his body. This is their work with the disbelievers. "Gharq" (violent drawing) is a noun standing in place of the verbal noun "ighraq" (violent drawing out), meaning: "And by those who pull out with violence." By ighraq is meant exaggeration in drawing.

Ibn Mas'ud said: The Angel of Death [and his helpers] pull it out from beneath every hair, from the nails, and from the roots of the feet [see: al-Tabari: 30/27], and he returns it into the body after pulling it out, until when it is almost coming out, he returns it into the body after pulling it out. This is their work with the disbelievers.

Muqatil said: The Angel of Death and his helpers pull out the souls of the disbelievers as a skewer with many prongs is pulled out of wet wool, and the soul comes out like one drowning in water.

Mujahid said: It is death, which pulls out the souls [see al-Tabari: 30/27].

al-Suddi said: It is the soul when it sinks into the chest [narrated by al-Tabari: 30/28].

al-Hasan, Qatadah and Ibn Kaysan said: It is the stars, which are pulled from horizon to horizon, rising and then setting [see al-Tabari: 30/28]. 'Ata' and 'Ikrimah said: It is the bows [see al-Tabari: 30/28]. It was also said: It is the warriors who shoot arrows [the author of Zad al-Masir said: 9/15, "al-Tha'labi related it"].

﴿And by those that glide swiftly with gliding﴾ — they are the angels who seize the souls of the believers, drawing them out gently and easily, then leave them until they rest, like a swimmer with something in the water who moves gently with it.

Mujāhid and Abū Ṣāliḥ said: they are the angels who descend from the sky swiftly, like a noble horse called sābiḥ when it hastens in its running.

It was also said: they are the horses of the warriors. Qatādah said: they are the stars and the sun [and the moon] [[Omitted from "B".]]. Allah the Most High said: ﴿each in an orbit swims along﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 33].

ʿAṭāʾ said: they are the ships.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 6–7:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿On the Day when the Quaking One quakes﴾ means the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula), by which everything trembles and is shaken, and by which all creation [in "b" it reads "al-khalq" (creation)] dies.

﴿Followed by the Second, the Following One﴾: this is the second blast, which follows the first, and between them is a period of forty years.

Qatadah said: "They are two cries. The first causes everything to die, and the other brings everything back to life by the permission of Allah, Exalted and Majestic." [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/31.]

Mujahid said: "The Quaking One: the earth and the mountains are shaken. The Following One: when the sky is split asunder, and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed into a single crushing." [See al-Tabari: 30/32.] ʿAta' said: "al-Rajifa is the Resurrection (al-qiyama), and al-Radifa is the Raising (al-ba'th)." The root of rajfa is sound and movement.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us, Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Harun [in "a" it reads "Muhammad ibn Ibrahim", and the name of his father Harun has probably dropped out; he is Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Ibrahim as in "Tahdhib al-Tahdhib"] al-Hadrami narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, Qabisa ibn ʿUqba narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAqil, from al-Tufayl ibn Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise when a quarter of the night had passed, and he would say: "O people, remember Allah, remember Allah. The Quaking One has come, followed by the Following One. Death has come with what is in it, death has come with what is in it."
[[Omitted from "a": "remember Allah, remember Allah." The hadith is recorded by al-Tirmidhi in Sifat al-Qiyama: 7/152-153, who said, "This is a hasan hadith," and al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/421, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Part of it is also narrated by Imam Ahmad: 5/136, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya: 1/256, and al-Albani graded it hasan in Silsilat al-Ahadith, no. (954), 2/675.]]

﴿Hearts that Day will be fearful﴾: frightened, anxious, agitated. The word *al-wajīf* is used of a fast gait because of its intense jolting, and it is said: *wajafa al-qalb wa-wajaba wujūfan wa-wajīfan wa-wujūban wa-wajīban* (the heart throbbed and pounded). Mujahid said: "Fearful." Al-Suddi said: "Displaced from their places." Its parallel is the verse ﴿when the hearts rise up to the throats﴾ [Ghafir: 18].

﴿Their eyes will be humbled﴾: humiliated, abased, like His saying ﴿humbled, cowed by humiliation﴾ [al-Shura: 45], and the rest of the verse.

﴿They say﴾: meaning the deniers of the Resurrection, when it is said to them that you will be resurrected after death: ﴿Shall we really be returned to our former state?﴾, that is, to the original condition and the beginning of the matter, so that we become living again after death as we were before? The Arabs say: *rajaʿa fulānun fī ḥāfiratihi*, meaning he returned by the way he came. *Al-ḥāfirah* among them is a term for the beginning of a thing, [and the beginning of a thing].[[Omitted in manuscript B.]]

Some said: *al-ḥāfirah* is the surface of the earth in which their graves are dug, and it was called *ḥāfirah* in the sense of *al-maḥfūrah* (the dug-out), like His saying ﴿a pleasing life﴾, meaning a pleasing [i.e. pleased-with] life.

It is also said: it was called *ḥāfirah* because it is the resting place of the hooves [*al-ḥawāfir*],[[In manuscript B: al-ḥāfir.]] meaning: Shall we really be returned to the earth so that we are raised as a new creation walking upon it? Ibn Zayd said: *al-ḥāfirah* is the Fire.

﴿Even when we are decayed bones?﴾ Nafi', Ibn ʿAmir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read *a-innā* as an interrogative and *idhā* without an interrogative. Abu Ja'far differed from them. [The rest] read both with the interrogative. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu ʿAmr read *ʿiẓāman nākhiratan* (hollow bones). The others read *nakhiratan*. Both are dialectal variants, like *al-ṭamiʿ* and *al-ṭāmiʿ*, and *al-ḥadhir* and *al-ḥādhir*. Their meaning is "decayed." Some people distinguished between them, saying: *al-nakhirah* is the decayed, and *al-nākhirah* is the hollow one through which the wind passes and whistles, that is, it makes a sound.

﴿They say﴾: meaning the deniers, ﴿That, then, would be a losing return﴾: a failed, disappointing return. That is, if we are sent back after death, we will indeed suffer loss through what befalls us after death.

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil (al-Baghawi), commentary on Surah 79, verses 21–30:**

﴿Then he denied﴾, that they were from God, ﴿and disobeyed﴾. ﴿Then he turned away﴾, meaning he turned his back and withdrew from faith. ﴿He strove﴾, meaning he worked at corruption on the earth.

﴿Then he gathered﴾, meaning he assembled his people and his soldiers. ﴿Then he called out﴾ once they had gathered.

﴿And said, "I am your lord, the most high."﴾ There is no lord above me. It is also said that he meant the idols are lords, and I am your lord and their lord.

﴿So God seized him, the seizing of the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: God punished him, making him an example (nakal) for the Hereafter and for the former life, that is, in this world by drowning and in the Hereafter by the Fire. [[See al-Tabari: 30/42.]]

Mujahid and a group of the exegetes said: by "the Hereafter and the first" he meant the two utterances of Pharaoh: his saying, "I know of no god for you other than myself" [al-Qasas: 38], and his saying, ﴿I am your lord, the most high﴾. Between them were forty years. [[See al-Tabari: 30/41.]]

﴿Indeed in that﴾, that which was done to Pharaoh when he denied and disobeyed, ﴿is a lesson﴾, an admonition ﴿for whoever fears﴾ God, Mighty and Majestic. Then He addressed those who deny the Resurrection, saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or the sky?﴾ That is, is your creation after death more difficult in your estimation and calculation, or the sky? Both are the same in God's power, as in His saying: "The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind" [Ghafir: 57]. Then He described the creation of the sky, saying: ﴿He built it﴾, ﴿He raised its height﴾, its ceiling, ﴿and made it level﴾, without any cracks [and without any splits] [[Omitted from manuscript "B".]] or fissures.

﴿And He darkened its night﴾, made it dark. Al-ghatsh and al-ghabsh mean darkness. ﴿And brought out its forenoon﴾, meaning He made its daylight and its light appear and become manifest. He attributed both to the sky because both darkness and light descend from the sky.

﴿And the earth, after that﴾, after the creation of the sky, ﴿He spread out﴾, meaning He extended it; al-dahw means spreading. Ibn Abbas said: God created the earth with its sustenance without spreading it out before the sky. Then He turned to the sky and made it into seven heavens, and afterward He spread out the earth ﴿after that﴾.

It is also said that the meaning is: "and the earth along with that He spread out," as in His saying, Mighty and Majestic: "Violent, and moreover, base-born" [al-Qalam: 13], meaning "along with that."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 79, verses 31–44:**

﴿He brought forth from it its water and its pasture, and the mountains He set firmly, as provision for you and your livestock. So when the Great Calamity comes﴾: meaning the second blast, in which is the Resurrection, and the Hour is established. The Hour is called "*al-ṭāmmah*" (the Calamity) because it overwhelms every terrifying matter, rising above them and submerging everything else. Among the Arabs, *al-ṭāmmah* is the calamity that cannot be withstood.

﴿On the Day when man will remember what he strove for﴾: what he did in the world of good and evil.

﴿And Hellfire is made apparent to whoever sees﴾: Muqatil said, "Its covering will be removed, and the creation will look upon it."

﴿As for him who transgressed﴾: in his disbelief.

﴿And preferred the worldly life﴾: over the Hereafter.

﴿Indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge. But as for him who feared the standing before his Lord and restrained the soul from desire﴾: from the forbidden things that it craves. Muqatil said, "This is the man who intends to commit disobedience, then remembers his standing for reckoning, and so he abandons it."

﴿Indeed, Paradise will be his refuge. They ask you about the Hour: when will be its arrival?﴾: when will be its appearance and its establishment.

﴿In what are you [concerned] with its mention?﴾: you have no part in its knowledge or its mention, that is, you do not know it.

﴿To your Lord is its finality﴾: that is, the ultimate knowledge of it is with Allah.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 79, verse 45–46:

﴿Verily, you are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ Abu Ja'far recited "mundhiru" (مُنْذِرٌ) with tanwin, meaning: [Verily, you are] [[Omitted from "B".]] one who warns those who fear its establishment. That is, your warning benefits only those who fear it.

﴿As if they,﴾ meaning the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿on the day they see it,﴾ i.e., witness it on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿will not have remained﴾ in the world, and it is said: in their graves, ﴿except for an evening or its morning.﴾ Al-Farra' said: [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 3/234.]] "The evening has no forenoon; rather, the forenoon (al-duha) is the early part of the day. But it is a common usage of the Arabs to say: 'I will come to you in the evening or its morning (ghadatuha),' meaning: the last day or its first." Its parallel is His saying: ﴿As if they, on the day they see what they are promised, had not remained except an hour of a day﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].
